title: Legacy invocation route heuristics and namespace canonicalization
creator: Jordan Kim
description:
Problem: Customers using legacy 'function' invocation (old SDKs / on-prem agents) and workloads written against OpenAI-style 'tools' face brittle failures during rollouts. The platform must correctly route invocations to compatible runtime handlers while preserving streaming behavior and structured output expectations. This ticket defines and implements a lightweight routing heuristic + namespace canonicalization layer that sits in the request ingress, resolves tool/function names across versions, and chooses the appropriate runtime handling path (stream-native vs batch/non-stream).

Scope:
- Resolve naming mismatches (e.g., camelCase vs snake_case, punctuation, prefix/suffix aliases) using a configurable fuzzy matcher and canonical registry.
- Prefer exact-namespace matches when present (customer-scoped tool registries override global aliases).
- Route streaming-capable requests to stream-enabled model variants; for legacy handlers that do not support streaming, apply an adaptive stream-to-chunk fallback with per-request backpressure.
- Emit explicit telemetry (decision reason, matched alias, fallback used) so Console engineers and customers can audit routing decisions.

Out of scope: deep contract translation (parameter coercion beyond name mapping) and long-term schema evolution for tools (handled in separate 'tool-contract-evolution' epic).
acceptance_criteria: Ingress layer implements fuzzy name matcher with configurable threshold and deterministic tie-breaker rules
Namespace precedence respected: customer-local > project > global aliases
Requests marked as streaming are routed to a stream-capable handler if available, otherwise fall back to chunked responses with correct chunk boundaries and finalization event
Telemetry emitted for every routing decision (alias, score, chosen handler) and visible in Console trace/route dashboard
Unit and integration tests cover: exact match, alias match, ambiguous ties, streaming->non-stream fallback, and namespace overrides
Migration plan documented with a rollout canary and automatic revert on error spike (>1% 5xx increase)
Performance overhead <2ms median added latency for best-case exact matches on p99 traffic profile
tasks: Design fuzzy-matcher primitives (tokenization, normalization, scoring) - draft complete
Implement matcher in ingress (Go) and expose config flags for threshold/tiebreak
Implement routing policy: namespace precedence, streaming capability check, fallback strategy
Add telemetry hooks and Console trace fields (route_reason, alias_score, handler_id)
Write unit tests for matcher and routing; integration test using local runtime harness
Create canary rollout: 5% traffic, 24h observation, automated revert on error spike
Write migration doc and notices for customers with legacy functions
comments: 2025-02-11 - Jordan Kim: Prototype fuzzy matcher implemented in ingress branch 'feat/route-heuristics'. Early results: exact matches unchanged; aliases matched with mean score 0.82 for common variants.

2025-02-12 - PM review (Ravi Singh): Requested stronger namespace precedence — customer-local registries must be immutable during canary. Also asked for explicit opt-out label for customers wanting original behavior.
2025-02-14 - Design (Maya Alvarez): UX note - Console should show both the caller-supplied name and canonical name to avoid confusion. Added to telemetry tasks.

2025-02-16 - Aisha Patel: Integration test discovered an edge case: multi-word tool names with punctuation (e.g., 'send-email!') normalized to 'send_email' but collide with 'sendEmail' alias. Decided to enforce deterministic tie-breaker favoring exact ascii-normalized matches first, then score.
2025-02-18 - Security (Liam O'Connor): Confirmed no new sensitive data surface; telemetry will avoid logging parameter values. Approved.
2025-02-19 - Aisha Patel: Performance note - initial Go matcher added ~3.4ms median on non-hot path. Optimized tokenization reduced to ~1.2ms. Goal to get <2ms remains.
2025-02-20 - Jordan Kim: Preparing PR for routing + telemetry. Next: add streaming fallback integration with chunk finalization event and canary config.
risks: False positives in fuzzy matching could route to incorrect handlers; mitigated by conservative default threshold and canary
Streaming fallback may alter latency profile and lead to client-side timeouts for some SDKs; mitigation: explicit opt-out and SDK patch notes
Telemetry volume increase; mitigation: sample non-error cases at 1% and full capture on routed-errors
notes: Implementation language: Go (ingress) + small runtime flag in serving runtime to advertise stream-capability
We will reuse the existing canonical tool registry service; add alias metadata and namespace ownership fields
Customer rollback: add feature-flag per-customer to disable heuristic-based routing immediately
